importance_ranking.reason: Buyers arrive with a defined structural application (solar mounting, canopy, shed) and immediately filter by product type, span/width, alloy grade, and finish — without matching specs the listing cannot be evaluated for project fit. Custom-fabricated structures are non-interchangeable across applications; wrong spec = project non-compliance.

Visual sub-type variation is extreme — a solar monorail, a pergola, a space frame, and a warehouse truss are visually unrecognisable from each other by title alone. Buyers use the image to confirm product type before reading any spec, and to assess fabrication quality and finish.

Price varies substantially with alloy grade, span, finish, and product type — a per-kg or per-watt rate is meaningless without the spec context. Indian B2B buyers (solar EPC contractors, shed fabricators) are price-aggressive and compare rates across sellers once spec equivalence is confirmed; listed price is a budget entry point for project costing.

importance_ranking.brand_important_reason: No dominant consumer-facing brand with buyer recall exists in Indian aluminium structural fabrication — buyers search by spec, application, and price, not manufacturer name; ISO/BIS certification and fabrication track record matter but are not brand signals.
importance_ranking.reason: Solar EPC contractors and construction buyers evaluate manufacturer capability, BIS/IS:875 compliance, installation support, and project track record during vendor shortlisting — seller identity is a qualification gate after spec and price match, not a primary scan signal.

importance_ranking.unit_note: Solar mounting sub-segment also uses per watt (₹/W) for system-level quotes and per piece/set for standard monorail kits; rail sections sold per metre. Unit must be shown because per kg, per watt, per piece, and per metre are all active in this MCAT and price cannot be compared without knowing the unit basis.
importance_ranking.reason: Unit ambiguity is a real and material risk — the same product type can be quoted per kg, per watt, per piece, or per metre by different sellers, making price comparison impossible without unit disclosure.

top_configurator_specs.reason: Defines what the structure IS — a solar mounting structure, pergola, greenhouse, or warehouse shed are non-interchangeable across buyer applications and carry fundamentally different price points, material requirements, and compliance standards.

Span is the primary dimensional configurator for structural pricing — material weight, engineering complexity, and fabrication cost scale directly with span, making it the largest single driver of per-kg or per-project price variation within any product type.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Alloy grade (6061 vs 6063 vs 6082) determines structural strength, extrudability, and compliance with IS:736/IS:737 — solar EPC and construction buyers specify alloy grade to confirm load-bearing capacity and BIS/MNRE eligibility.

Solar mounting and structural buyers must confirm IS:875 wind zone compliance and design load rating before procurement — a structure rated for Wind Zone II cannot be used in Wind Zone IV without re-engineering, making this a hard shortlisting gate.

Solar EPC buyers specify system capacity in kW (e.g., 10 kW, 100 kW, 1 MW) and shed/canopy buyers specify floor area or load in sq ft or MT — without this, sellers cannot confirm whether their standard structure fits the buyer's project scale.

top_rfq_specs.reason: Application routes the RFQ to sellers who fabricate the specific structure type — a solar structure seller cannot supply a greenhouse frame, and misrouted RFQs waste both buyer and seller time.

Surface finish (powder coated vs anodized vs mill finish) affects both aesthetics and corrosion protection specification — sellers need this to confirm they can supply the required finish and to price the coating process accurately.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Sellers need alloy grade to confirm structural compliance and BIS certification eligibility — a buyer specifying 6061 T6 for a high-load application cannot be served by a seller who only stocks 6063 T5.
Sellers need to know the system size (kW for solar, sq ft for canopy/shed) to determine whether their standard fabrication capacity and structural design covers the buyer's requirement.
